title: Death toll from Nepal-China border floods rises to 1,410, with thousands still missing - TRT World
description: Death toll from Nepal-China border floods rises to 1,410, with thousands still missing  TRT World
publisher.title: TRT World
full_article:
Nepali authorities have retrieved another 10 bodies in flood-hit areas as the death toll from devastating floods and mudslides that struck the Nepal-China border late last month climbed to 1,410, with over 5,650 still missing, official statistics showed on Wednesday.

Of those missing, 848 are foreigners, according to official figures from both Nepal and China.

Some 1,367 bodies have been recovered from flood-stricken districts in Nepal, while 5,132 people, including 587 foreigners, remain missing, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

Over 13,600 people have so far been rescued, including as recently as last weekend.

एखन धरि 13,600 सं बेसी लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि, जाहि मे हाल मे पिछला सप्ताहांत मे सेहो शामिल अछि.

title: Nepal seeks survivors two weeks after deadly floods - Arab News
description: Nepal seeks survivors two weeks after deadly floods  Arab News
publisher.title: Arab News
full_article:
KATMANDU, Nepal: Nepali rescuers clung to hopes of finding survivors trapped in hydropower tunnels on Wednesday, two weeks after deadly flooding triggered by a glacial mountain collapse.

The August 26 tsunami-like surge of water, mud and debris, which began on the China-Nepal border, has killed more than 1,410 people and left 5,651 missing.

“The rescue and search work in the tunnels at Trishuli 3A, 3B and Chilime hydropower projects is ongoing,” Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.

In Nepal, 1,367 bodies have been recovered and 5,132 people are missing, according to Kathmandu’s disaster authority on Wednesday. In China, 43 people are dead and 519 missing, according to state media.

Hundreds of foreigners are among the missing, as well as hundreds of hydropower workers.

Three people were rescued from deep inside tunnels – two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday.

But there has been no official confirmation of further survivors since then.

Thousands of people displaced by the diaster are living in camps, and the charity Save the Children said as many as 540 children had been separated from their parents.

While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melt worldwide and increasing the risk of such disasters.

Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people that has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, has said reconstruction could cost billions of dollars.

title: What 13 minutes in Nepal can teach us about acting before disaster strikes - The New Humanitarian
description: What 13 minutes in Nepal can teach us about acting before disaster strikes  The New Humanitarian
publisher.title: The New Humanitarian
full_article:
Rajendra Dawadi had to make a decision in an instant. Warned that floodwaters were racing towards his school in Nepal’s Trishuli Valley, the headmaster had no way of knowing how much time he had, nor whether the floodwaters would reach his school. He did not hesitate and evacuated more than 900 students and 16 staff to higher ground.

Approximately 13 minutes later, a wall of water, mud, and debris swept through the area, destroying the school.

Dawadi acted before he knew for certain what was coming. His calculation was simple. If the warning proved wrong, his students would miss a day of school. If it was right and he did nothing, hundreds of children could die.

The instinct to act while there is still time, despite uncertainty, is at the heart of anticipatory action. Investing ahead of known risks has been shown to save lives and reduce losses. But acting ahead requires accepting that some forecasts will never provide complete certainty, and that waiting to act can carry far higher consequences.

Nepal shows what formal systems can and cannot do

Nepal is hardly a newcomer to acting ahead of disasters. The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology introduced the flood early warning system in the 1990s, combining both high-tech river level monitoring stations with simpler community-based systems for detecting rising waters and disseminating warnings.

In 2022, the government held the first national dialogue on anticipatory action, and this year endorsed a national policy. Humanitarian organisations have been experimenting with anticipatory approaches for more than a decade, releasing pre-arranged emergency funding at least twice for flood response.

The August disaster, however, fell outside of the mainly weather-related monsoon flooding that these mechanisms were designed to anticipate and warn against. A huge section of glacier and surrounding bedrock collapsed high in Tibet, sending ice, rock, and debris into the river system and generating a catastrophic flood that travelled nearly 100 kilometres downstream. Automatic monitoring stations along the upper Bhotekoshi River were meant to detect rising water and alert communities downstream, but the flood moved so quickly that monitoring stations inside Nepal were destroyed before they could transmit a warning. The community-level river gauges that gradually measured river behaviour were also too slow for a flood travelling at an average speed of 193 kilometres per hour.

Some of these limitations were already understood. A 2023 review of Nepal’s anticipatory action experience raised concerns about the reliability of forecasts and called for greater flexibility to combine scientific triggers with human judgement and changing conditions on the ground. A later study in 2025 found their early warning messaging system frequently did not prompt the necessary actions to save lives and protect assets.

What happened at Dawadi’s school shows why this matters. The warning that saved Dawadi’s students did not come through the formal monitoring or early warning system. A relative upstream called the school accountant. Teachers received calls from family and friends. A parent arrived to collect her child. Dawadi ordered the evacuation. Teachers, parents, and others then helped get the children uphill. Many others were not so fortunate. Elsewhere along the flood’s path, people had almost no time to react.

Forecasting and early warning technology remain essential, but they have to be matched by readiness at the community level – evacuation plans, trusted communication networks, prepared local institutions and people able to act when information arrives.

Those community connections are part of the infrastructure of disaster readiness. I saw their importance when I lived in Japan and studied how the country prepares for disasters in 2019. Japan is famous for its enormous investment in seawalls, flood defences, earthquake-resistant buildings and sophisticated warning systems. But some of its most important investments are far simpler.

Children learn about disaster risk from kindergarten. Communities practise evacuations. Families are encouraged to have a go-bag ready at all times. Residents identify neighbours who may need help. Survivors share their experiences with communities facing similar hazards.

Japan also shows the limits of relying too heavily on infrastructure and more formal warning systems. During severe 2018 flooding in Mabi, a district in western Japan situated near two rivers, embankments were overwhelmed and mobile-phone warnings failed to reach some of the elderly people most at risk. Research after the Mabi flood and the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami found that some residents delayed evacuating because they believed physical defences would protect them.

Forecasting and early warning technology remain essential, but they have to be matched by readiness at the community level – evacuation plans, trusted communication networks, prepared local institutions and people able to act when information arrives. These investments may be less visible than satellites, monitoring stations or dams, but they can determine whether a warning actually saves a life.

Schools are an important part of that community readiness. My research on education and anticipatory action with the Geneva Global Hub for Education in Emergencies in 2024 found much the same thing that Dawadi’s experience demonstrates: Schools can play a critical role in turning early warnings into action. They reach children and families every day, while teachers are often trusted community leaders who can communicate risks, organise evacuations, and connect formal warning systems with local knowledge. Disaster education also gives children knowledge they take home and carry into adulthood, strengthening the ability of entire communities to respond to future crises.

Governments, donors, and aid agencies must become more comfortable spending money before they can be certain a crisis will unfold as forecast.

Scientists are still grappling with how to predict rock-ice avalanches like the one in Nepal. But as glacial flooding increases as a result of global warming, they warn that these events are expected to be more common around the world. Anticipatory approaches and funding will need to adapt to include these emerging risks while investing more in the local institutions and relationships that can turn warnings into action.

Yet humanitarian financing still runs overwhelmingly in the opposite direction. Ninety-nine percent of international humanitarian funding still flows after disasters happen and only about 12% of total anticipatory action funding between 2022 and 2023 involved those organisations closest to communities. In a time of collapsing budgets and hyper-prioritisation, it is urgent to rethink whether scarce resources are being deployed where – and when – they can have the greatest effect.

Some actions may prove unnecessary. Sometimes, supplies will be moved for a flood that changes course. Cash may be released ahead of a drought that proves less severe than expected. Schools may close for storms that never arrive. That does not make those decisions bad ones. Governments, donors, and aid agencies must become more comfortable spending money before they can be certain a crisis will unfold as forecast. The cost of acting unnecessarily can be far smaller than the cost of acting too late.

Dawadi understood that tradeoff.

राजेन्द्र दावादी के पल भर में निर्णय लेबय पड़लनि। नेपालक त्रिशूली उपत्यका मे बाढ़िक पानि हुनकर स्कूल दिस दौड़ि रहल अछि से चेतावनी देलनि, हेडमास्टर केँ ई बुझबाक कोनो उपाय नहि छलनि जे हुनका लग कतेक समय छनि, आ ने बाढ़िक पानि हुनकर स्कूल धरि पहुँचत कि नहि. ओ कोनो संकोच नहि केलनि आ 900 सं बेसी छात्र आ 16 कर्मचारी के ऊँच मैदान पर ल गेलाह.

लगभग 13 मिनट बाद एहि इलाका मे पानि, थाल आ मलबा क देबाल आबि गेल, जाहि स स्कूल तबाह भ गेल।

दावादी ओकरा निश्चित रूपसँ बुझबासँ पहिने काज केलक जे की आबि रहल अछि । हुनकर गणना सरल छलनि। जँ चेतावनी गलत साबित होइत तँ ओकर विद्यार्थी सभ एक दिन स्कूलसँ छूटि जाइत छल । जँ ठीक रहैत आ ओ किछु नहि करितथि तँ सैकड़ो बच्चा मरि सकैत छल ।

अनिश्चितताक बादो समय रहैत काज करबाक वृत्ति पूर्वानुमानात्मक क्रियाक मूल मे होइत छैक । ज्ञात जोखिम सं आगू निवेश सं जान बचाबय आ नुकसान कम करय के बात कहल गेल अछि. लेकिन आगू बढ़ै लेली ई बात क॑ स्वीकार करना जरूरी छै कि कुछ पूर्वानुमान स॑ कहियो पूरा निश्चय नै मिलतै, आरू काम करै के इंतजार करला स॑ एकरऽ परिणाम कहीं अधिक होय सकै छै ।

नेपाल ई देखाबैत अछि जे औपचारिक व्यवस्था की क' सकैत अछि आ की नहि क' सकैत अछि

आपदा स आगू काज करबा मे नेपाल शायदे कोनो नव आगंतुक अछि। जल विज्ञान आरू मौसम विभाग न॑ १९९० के दशक म॑ बाढ़ केरऽ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली शुरू करलकै, जेकरा म॑ बढ़तऽ पानी के पता लगाबै आरू चेतावनी फैलाबै लेली उच्च तकनीक वाला नदी स्तर प॑ निगरानी दूनू स्टेशनऽ क॑ सरल समुदाय आधारित प्रणाली के साथ जोड़लऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

2022 म॑ सरकार न॑ पूर्वानुमानित कार्रवाई प॑ पहलऽ राष्ट्रीय संवाद करलकै, आरू ई साल एगो राष्ट्रीय नीति के समर्थन करलकै । मानवीय संगठन एक दशक स॑ भी अधिक समय स॑ प्रत्याशित दृष्टिकोण के प्रयोग करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ बाढ़ के प्रतिक्रिया लेली कम स॑ कम दू बार पूर्व निर्धारित आपातकालीन फंडिंग जारी करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

अगस्त केरऽ आपदा, हालांकि, मुख्य रूप स॑ मौसम स॑ जुड़लऽ मानसून केरऽ बाढ़ स॑ बाहर गिरी गेलै जेकरऽ पूर्वानुमान आरू चेतावनी लेली ई तंत्रऽ के डिजाइन करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । तिब्बत में ग्लेशियर आरू आसपास केरऽ बेडरोक केरऽ एगो विशाल खंड ऊँचऽ भाग में गिरी गेलै, जेकरा स॑ बर्फ, चट्टान आरू मलबा नदी प्रणाली में भेजलऽ गेलै आरू एक भयावह बाढ़ पैदा होय गेलै जे लगभग १०० किलोमीटर नीचें गेलै । ऊपरी भोटेकोशी नदी के किनारे स्वचालित निगरानी स्टेशन के उद्देश्य बढ़ैत पानि के पता लगाबय आ नीचा के समुदाय के सचेत करय के छल, मुदा बाढ़ एतेक तेजी सं बढ़ल जे नेपाल के भीतर के निगरानी स्टेशन के चेतावनी संचारित करय सं पहिने नष्ट क देल गेल. समुदाय स्तरीय नदी गेज जे धीरे-धीरे नदी के व्यवहार के मापैत छल, ओ सेहो बहुत धीमा छल जे बाढ़ के औसत गति 193 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटा के गति सं चलैत छल.

एहि मे स किछु सीमा पहिने स बुझल गेल छल। नेपाल केरऽ प्रत्याशित कार्य अनुभव केरऽ २०२३ केरऽ समीक्षा म॑ पूर्वानुमान केरऽ विश्वसनीयता के बारे म॑ चिंता पैदा करलऽ गेलै आरू वैज्ञानिक ट्रिगर क॑ मानवीय निर्णय आरू जमीन प॑ बदलतऽ परिस्थिति के साथ जोड़ै लेली अधिक लचीलापन के आह्वान करलऽ गेलै । बाद मँ 2025 मँ एगो अध्ययन मँ पता चललै कि हुनकऽ पूर्व चेतावनी संदेश प्रणाली अक्सर जान बचाबै आरू संपत्ति के सुरक्षा लेली आवश्यक कार्रवाई लेली प्रेरित नै करै छै ।

दावादी’क स्कूल मे जे भेलै से ई दर्शाबै छै कि ई बात कियैक मायने रखै छै. जे चेतावनी दवादी के छात्र के बचा लेलक ओ औपचारिक निगरानी या पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली के माध्यम सं नहि आयल छल. अपस्ट्रीम के एकटा रिश्तेदार स्कूल के एकाउंटेंट के फोन केलक। शिक्षक कए परिवार आ मित्र स फोन आयल। एकटा अभिभावक अपन बच्चा के बटोरय लेल पहुंचल। दावादी खाली करबाक आदेश देलनि। तखन शिक्षक, अभिभावक, आ अन्य लोकनि बच्चा सभ केँ चढ़ाबय मे मदद केलनि। कतेको आन लोकक ओतेक सौभाग्य नहि छल। बाढ़ि’क बाट मे आन ठाम लोक केँ प्रतिक्रिया देबाक समय लगभग नहि छल.

पूर्वानुमान आ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रौद्योगिकी आवश्यक बनल छै, मुदा ओकर मिलान समुदाय स्तर पर तत्परता सं करनाय होयत छै – खाली करय कें योजना, विश्वसनीय संचार नेटवर्क, तैयार स्थानीय संस्थान आ जानकारी आवय पर कार्य करय मे सक्षम लोग.

ओ सामुदायिक कनेक्शन आपदा तत्परता कें बुनियादी ढाँचा कें हिस्सा छै. हम जापान में रहैत जखन एकर महत्व देखलहुं आ अध्ययन केलहुं जे 2019 में देश आपदा के तैयारी कोना करैत अछि.जापान समुद्री देवाल, बाढ़ि सं बचाव, भूकंप प्रतिरोधी भवन आ परिष्कृत चेतावनी प्रणाली में अपन भारी निवेश के लेल प्रसिद्ध अछि. मुदा एकर किछु महत्वपूर्ण निवेश कहीं बेसी सरल अछि।

बच्चाक कें बालवाड़ी सं आपदा कें जोखिम कें बारे मे पता चलएयत छै. समुदाय खाली करय के अभ्यास करैत अछि। परिवारक कें प्रोत्साहित कैल जायत छै की हर समय गो-बैग तैयार रहय. निवासी पड़ोसी कें पहचान करएयत छै, जेकरा मदद कें जरूरत भ सकएय छै. बचि गेल लोगक अपन अनुभवक कें ओय समुदायक कें संग साझा करएयत छै जे समान खतरा कें सामना करएयत छै.

जापान बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू अधिक औपचारिक चेतावनी प्रणाली प॑ बहुत जादा भरोसा करै के सीमा भी देखाबै छै । 2018 म॑ पश्चिमी जापान केरऽ एगो जिला माबी म॑ दू नदी के पास स्थित भयंकर बाढ़ के दौरान तटबंधऽ प॑ भारी पड़लऽ छेलै आरू मोबाइल-फोन के चेतावनी सबस॑ बेसी खतरा म॑ पड़लऽ कुछ बुजुर्ग लोगऽ तलक नै पहुँची सकलऽ छेलै । माबी बाढ़ आरू २०११ केरऽ महान पूर्वी जापान भूकंप आरू सुनामी के बाद के शोध म॑ पता चललै कि कुछ निवासी न॑ घरऽ स॑ बाहर निकलै म॑ देरी करलकै, कैन्हेंकि ओकरा मानना ​​छेलै कि भौतिक रक्षा स॑ ओकरऽ सुरक्षा मिलतै ।

पूर्वानुमान आ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रौद्योगिकी आवश्यक बनल छै, मुदा ओकर मिलान समुदाय स्तर पर तत्परता सं करनाय होयत छै – खाली करय कें योजना, विश्वसनीय संचार नेटवर्क, तैयार स्थानीय संस्थान आ जानकारी आवय पर कार्य करय मे सक्षम लोग. ई निवेश उपग्रह, निगरानी स्टेशन या बांध के तुलना म॑ कम दिखाई द॑ सकै छै, लेकिन ई ई तय करी सकै छै कि चेतावनी स॑ वास्तव म॑ जान बचै छै कि नै ।

स्कूल ओहि सामुदायिक तत्परता के एकटा महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा अछि. 2024 म॑ जेनेवा ग्लोबल हब फॉर एजुकेशन इन इमरजेंसी के साथ शिक्षा आरू प्रत्याशित कार्रवाई प॑ हमरऽ शोध म॑ बहुत कुछ वू ही मिललै जे दावादी केरऽ अनुभव स॑ पता चलै छै कि स्कूल जल्दी चेतावनी क॑ कार्रवाई म॑ बदलै म॑ अहम भूमिका निभा सकै छै । इ हर दिन बच्चाक आ परिवारक तइक पहुंचएयत छै, जखन कि शिक्षक अक्सर भरोसेमंद समुदायक कें नेता होयत छै जे जोखिम कें संवाद कयर सकएय छै, निकासी कें आयोजन कयर सकएय छै, आ औपचारिक चेतावनी प्रणाली कें स्थानीय ज्ञान सं जोड़ सकएय छै. आपदा शिक्षा बच्चाक कें ओ ज्ञान कें सेहो देयत छै जे ओ घर ल जायत छै आ वयस्कता मे ल जायत छै, जे भविष्य कें संकट कें जवाब देवय कें लेल पूरा समुदायक कें क्षमता कें मजबूत करयत छै.

सरकार, दाता, आ सहायता एजेंसी कें पैसा खर्च करय मे बेसि सहज होनाय आवश्यक छै, ओकरा सं पहिले कि ओ इ निश्चिंत भ सकय कि कोनों संकट पूर्वानुमान कें अनुसार खुलतय.

वैज्ञानिक एखनो एहि बात सं जूझि रहल छथिन्ह जे नेपाल मे जेना चट्टान-बर्फ के हिमस्खलन के भविष्यवाणी कोना कएल जाए. लेकिन जेना-जेना ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के परिणामस्वरूप हिमनदीय बाढ़ बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, वू चेतावनी दै छै कि ई घटना दुनिया भर म॑ अधिक होय के उम्मीद छै । प्रत्याशित दृष्टिकोण आ वित्तपोषण कें इ उभरैत जोखिम कें शामिल करय कें लेल अनुकूलित करय कें जरूरत होयत आ स्थानीय संस्थाक आ संबंधक मे बेसि निवेश करय कें होयत जे चेतावनी कें कार्यवाही मे बदल सकय छै.

तइयो मानवीय वित्तपोषण एखनो भारी मात्रा मे एकर विपरीत दिशा मे चलि रहल अछि। अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानवीय वित्तपोषण कें 99 प्रतिशत आपदाक कें बाद अखनी तइक बहय छै आ 2022 सं 2023 कें बीच कुल प्रत्याशित कार्यवाही कें वित्तपोषण कें मात्र लगभग 12% समुदायक कें सब सं नजदीकी संगठनक कें शामिल कैल गेलय. बजट केरऽ पतन आरू अति-प्राथमिकता केरऽ समय म॑ ई बात प॑ पुनर्विचार करना जरूरी छै कि दुर्लभ संसाधनऽ क॑ कहाँ – आरू कहिया – सबसें जादा प्रभाव डाल॑ सकै छै, तैनात करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै कि नै ।

किछु काज अनावश्यक साबित भ सकैत अछि। कखनो काल, बाढ़ि लेल आपूर्ति स्थानांतरित भ जायत जे मार्ग बदलि जायत। सूखा सं पहिने नकदी जारी भ सकैत अछि जे उम्मीद सं कम गंभीर साबित भ जाएत. स्कूल बंद भ सकैत अछि जे आंधी-तूफान कहियो नहि आबि सकैत अछि। जे ओहि निर्णय सभकेँ खराब नहि बना दैत अछि । सरकार, दाता, आ सहायता एजेंसी कें पैसा खर्च करय मे बेसि सहज होनाय आवश्यक छै, ओकरा सं पहिले कि ओ इ निश्चिंत भ सकय कि कोनों संकट पूर्वानुमान कें अनुसार खुलतय. अनावश्यक रूप स अभिनय करबाक लागत बहुत देर स अभिनय करबाक लागत स कहीं कम भ सकैत अछि।

full_article:
Nepali rescuers clung to hopes of finding survivors trapped in hydropower tunnels on Wednesday, two weeks after deadly flooding triggered by a glacial mountain collapse.

The August 26 tsunami-like surge of water, mud and debris, which began on the China-Nepal border, has killed more than 1,410 people and left 5,651 missing.

"The rescue and search work in the tunnels at Trishuli 3A, 3B and Chilime hydropower projects is ongoing," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.

In Nepal, 1,367 bodies have been recovered and 5,132 people are missing, its disaster authority said on Wednesday.

In China, 43 people are dead and 519 are missing, according to state media.

Hundreds of foreigners are among the missing, as well as hundreds of hydropower workers.

Three people were rescued from deep inside tunnels -- two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday.

But there has been no official confirmation of further survivors since then.

Thousands of people displaced by the disaster are living in camps, and the charity Save the Children said as many as 540 children had been separated from their parents.

Nepal police said they were taking extra care to ensure the safety of children and women in relief camps.

"We have become more vigilant in temporary holding centres in the affected areas where there are children, women or minority groups who could be victims of sexual abuse," said Nepal Police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.

"We have also started providing psychosocial counselling in different camps," he told AFP.

While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melt worldwide and increasing the risk of such disasters.

Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people that has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, has said reconstruction could cost billions of dollars.

Kafle said security personnel have involved community members to search for bodies feared buried under debris.

"We have started a special search campaign for missing bodies all across the Bhotekoshi river corridor," he said.

"We are also using drones to search for bodies."

चीन-नेपाल सीमा पर शुरू भेल 26 अगस्त के सुनामी सन पानि, थाल आ मलबा के उफान मे 1410 सं बेसी लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि आओर 5651 लोक लापता भ गेल अछि.

नेपाल सेनाके प्रवक्ता राजा राम बस्नेत एएफपीके बतौलनि जे, त्रिशुली ३ ए, ३ बी आ चिलिमे जलविद्युत परियोजनामे सुरंगमे बचाव आ खोज कार्य जारी अछि ।

नेपालमे १,३६७ शव बरामद भेल अछि आ ५,१३२ गोटे लापता अछि, ओकर आपदा प्राधिकरण बुधदिन जनौलक अछि ।

चीनमे ४३ गोटेके मृत्यु भेल अछि आ ५१९ गोटे लापता अछि ।

लापता मे सैकड़ों विदेशी के संग-संग सैकड़ों जलविद्युत मजदूर सेहो शामिल छथिन्ह.

गहींर भीतर सुरंग स तीन गोटे के बचाओल गेल -- शुक्रदिन दू गोटे नेपाली आ शनिदिन एकटा चीनी आदमी।

मुदा तकर बाद आओर बचि गेल लोक के आधिकारिक पुष्टि नहिं भेल अछि.

आपदा स॑ विस्थापित हजारों लोग कैंप म॑ रह॑ छै, आरू चैरिटी सेव द चिल्ड्रेन न॑ कहलकै कि ५४० बच्चा सिनी क॑ ओकरऽ माता-पिता स॑ अलग करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल पुलिस राहत शिविर मे बैसल बच्चा आ महिला के सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करय लेल अतिरिक्त सावधानी बरते रहल अछि।

नेपाल प्रहरी प्रवक्ता अबी नारायण काफ्ले कहलनि जे, प्रभावित क्षेत्र मे अस्थायी होल्डिंग केन्द्र मे हम सब बेसी सतर्क भ गेल छी जतय बच्चा, महिला या अल्पसंख्यक समूह अछि जे यौन शोषण के शिकार भ सकैत अछि।

ओ एएफपी स कहलथि जे हम सब अलग-अलग शिविर मे मनोसामाजिक परामर्श सेहो शुरू करि देलहुं अछि।

हिमनदी केरऽ पतन केरऽ सही कारण स्पष्ट नै छै, लेकिन जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण दुनिया भर म॑ हिमनदी केरऽ पिघलना म॑ तेजी आबी रहलऽ छै आरू ऐसनऽ आपदा के खतरा बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ।

तीन करोड़ लोगऽ के बहुत हद तक ग्रामीण राष्ट्र नेपाल न॑ कहल॑ छै कि ग्लोबल वार्मिंग क॑ बढ़ाबै वाला ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन म॑ बहुत कम योगदान देल॑ छै ।

काफ्ले कहलनि जे, सुरक्षाकर्मी समुदाय के सदस्य के शामिल क मलबा के नीचा गाड़ल आशंका वाला लाश के खोज केलक अछि।

ओ कहलनि जे, हम सब भोटेकोशी नदी गलियारा के चारू कात लापता लाश के विशेष खोज अभियान शुरू केने छी।

ओ कहलनि जे, हम सब लाश के खोजय लेल ड्रोन के उपयोग सेहो क रहल छी।

full_article:
By Joseph Campbell

DEVIGHAT, Nepal, Sept 9 (Reuters) - With ⁠roads ⁠and bridges destroyed and ⁠helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last ​month's devastating floods, Nepal’s army is turning to drones to deliver relief to ‌displaced people.

At least 1,367 people ‌are confirmed dead and more than 5,000 are missing in ⁠Nepal since ⁠a Himalayan glacier broke off near the Nepal-China border in ​late August and caused devastation along rivers further downstream.

“Most of our helicopters are busy with rescue operations. There is no other way to send food, essentials, ​medicine and fuel, except for drones, which are the best option to ⁠utilise, ⁠and we should prioritise ⁠them more,” ​said Santosh Budhathoki, a contract drone pilot for the Nepal army.

Drones are ​used over distances of ⁠up to 3 to 4 kilometres (2 to 2.5 miles) and can haul up to 60 kilograms (132 lbs) at a time and they are already making an impact for affected communities in dire need of aid, he ⁠said.

The army is now making around 10-16 aid deliveries a day ⁠with a fleet of four DJI FlyCart 100 drones, all donated from China as part of a recent aid package.

In addition to aid delivery, drones have also been used to move the bodies of flood victims in some affected areas, while reconnaissance drones have also been heavily used in search and rescue operations.

“We’ve been operating back and forth early in the morning. So yes, ⁠it is quite hectic, because we need to have this thing right now,” said Milan Pandey of the drone operating company, Airlift Technology.

“Nepal has this geography, this terrain where drones would be really ​faster, quicker and cheaper,” Pandey said.

(Reporting and writing by ​Joseph Campbell; Editing by Toby Chopra)

अगस्त के अंत में ⁠नेपाल-चीन सीमा के पास हिमालयी ग्लेशियर टूटि क आओर नीचा नदी के कात तबाही मचला के बाद स ⁠नेपाल में कम स कम 1367 लोक के मौत के पुष्टि भ गेल अछि आ 5000 स बेसी लोक लापता अछि।

नेपाली सेना केरऽ ठेका ड्रोन पायलट संतोष बुधाथोकी न॑ कहलकै कि हमरऽ अधिकांश हेलीकॉप्टर बचाव कार्य म॑ व्यस्त छै, ड्रोन के अलावा खाना, आवश्यक सामान, दवाई आरू ईंधन भेजै के दोसरऽ तरीका नै छै, जेकरऽ ⁠उपयोग करै के सबसें अच्छा विकल्प छै, ⁠आरू ओकरा ⁠ओकरा बेसी प्राथमिकता देना चाहियऽ ।

हुनी कहलकै कि ड्रोन के उपयोग ⁠३ स॑ ४ किलोमीटर (२ स॑ २.५ मील) तलक के दूरी प॑ करलऽ जाय छै आरू एक बार म॑ ६० किलोग्राम (१३२ पाउंड) तलक के दूरी प॑ खींच॑ सकै छै आरू ई पहल॑ स॑ ही सहायता के सख्त जरूरत वाला प्रभावित समुदाय लेली प्रभाव डाल॑ लगलऽ छै ।

सेना अब॑ रोजाना लगभग १०-१६ सहायता डिलीवरी करी रहलऽ छै ⁠4 डीजीआई फ्लाईकार्ट १०० ड्रोन के बेड़ा के साथ, जे सब चीन स॑ हाल केरऽ सहायता पैकेज के हिस्सा के रूप म॑ दान म॑ देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

सहायता वितरण के अलावा कुछ प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ बाढ़ पीड़ितऽ के शव क॑ ले जाय लेली भी ड्रोन के इस्तेमाल करलऽ गेलऽ छै, जबकि खोज आरू बचाव अभियान म॑ भी टोही ड्रोन के इस्तेमाल करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ड्रोन संचालन कंपनी एयरलिफ्ट टेक्नोलॉजी के मिलन पांडेय कहलनि जे, हम सब भोरे-भोर आगू-पाछू संचालित करैत रहलहुं अछि.त हाँ, ⁠ई काफी व्यस्तता अछि, किया कि हमरा सब लग एखन ई चीज हेबाक जरूरत अछि।

पाण्डेय कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे ई भूगोल अछि, ई इलाका अछि जतय ड्रोन सचमुच तेज, तेज आ सस्ता होयत।

(रिपोर्टिंग आ लेखन जोसेफ कैम्पबेल; संपादन टोबी चोपड़ा)

title: Sonoma nonprofit to host Sept. 22 fundraiser for victims of Nepal floods - Sonoma Index-Tribune
description: Sonoma nonprofit to host Sept. 22 fundraiser for victims of Nepal floods  Sonoma Index-Tribune
publisher.title: Sonoma Index-Tribune
full_article:
The Sherpa and Nepali community of Sonoma Valley is hosting a fundraiser to support relief and rescue efforts after floods in central Nepal killed more than 1,000 people, while thousands of others have gone missing.

The Himalayan Sherpa Club of Sonoma, a local nonprofit, will host a free event with wine and food at 4:30 p.m. Sept. 22 at the Sonoma Veterans Memorial Hall, 126 First St. W. in Sonoma.

“Basically, everything is free and they can donate whatever they can from their heart,” said Pemba Sherpa, a Sonoma resident of over 20 years and a member of The Himalayan Sherpa Club of Sonoma.

Various restaurants, such as Grape, Sonoma Grille, Everest Indian Restaurant from Petaluma and Yak and Yeti from Napa, will be serving food at the fundraiser.

The Sherpas are an ethnic group that migrated from Tibet to Nepal years ago.

According to Pemba Sherpa, several members of the community who now call the city of Sonoma home are from the Mount Everest and Makalu regions in the Himalayas and some of these people still have family, friends and relatives in Nepal and its surrounding regions.

“We have American families that are more worried than us because they are all worried about how we are doing and our families and friends are affected,” Sherpa said.

The nonprofit, in coordination with the California Sherpa Association in the Bay Area, will donate all the funds to the Nepali government’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund.

Sherpa said the nonprofit is hoping to raise $150,000 to $200,000.

title: AS Roma and World Food Programme join forces to support Nepal - AS Roma

full_article:
For the showdown between Fenerbahce and Roma on 10 September in Istanbul on the opening matchday of the league phase of the Champions League, the visitors will take to the pitch with the World Food Programme (WFP) logo on the front of their shirts.

Floods and landslides have severely affected several areas of Nepal, leaving entire communities cut off from the rest of the country. Around 43,000 people are in need of urgent humanitarian assistance. The WFP is supporting the emergency response by providing food assistance and logistical support to reach the worst-affected and most isolated communities.

AS Roma would like to thank Eurobet.live for contributing to the realization of this initiative, which will shine a spotlight on the emergency in Nepal and the work of the World Food Programme.



Roma’s support will continue long after the final whistle is blown. The shirts worn by Gian Piero Gasperini’s players during the match will be auctioned, with all funds raised going towards supporting the people of Nepal through the WFP’s relief efforts.

Fans can also contribute through ShareTheMeal, the WFP’s platform.

A small gesture can help provide food and assistance to those who need it most.

title: Doctor with University of Minnesota ties declared missing in Nepal floods - 5 EYEWITNESS NEWS
description: Doctor with University of Minnesota ties declared missing in Nepal floods  5 EYEWITNESS NEWS
publisher.title: 5 EYEWITNESS NEWS
full_article:
A doctor who recently completed a fellowship at the University of Minnesota and three of his family members were declared missing on Tuesday after catastrophic flooding in Nepal two weeks ago.

In a social media post, the University of Minnesota Department of Orthopedic Surgery said Dr. Ishan Patel traveled to Nepal on a pilgrimage after graduating from its Adult Reconstructive Fellowship. He was accompanied by his wife, Akansha Patel; his mother, Shilpa Patel; and his father-in-law, Umesh Kumar.

According to the university department, available information indicated the family was staying at a hotel when flooding struck the region. Floodwaters swept away the hotel and all four were declared missing.

The flooding followed a glacier collapse near the Nepal-China border on Aug. 26, triggering a massive torrent of water and mud that devastated mountain communities.

On Monday, the Associated Press reported more than 1,300 people died in Nepal and Tibet, and about 5,000 others remained missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency. Nepal observed a national day of mourning on Monday.

“This situation continues to evolve, and recovery efforts in the region are ongoing,” the university department said. “Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with Dr. Patel, his family, and all those affected by this tragedy.”

title: Relief efforts continue following Nepali mudslides - The Pathway
description: Relief efforts continue following Nepali mudslides  The Pathway
publisher.title: The Pathway
full_article:
GRAND JUNCTION, Colo. (BP) – The situation in Nepal is much more dire than news reports indicate, says the pastor of an unnamed Christian church in Kathmandu and leader of a Nepali network of more than five hundred churches across Nepal.

“Eyewitnesses tell us that more than 25 to 30 thousand people died but the government has only reported 12,500,” the Nepali pastor on Sept. 5 texted Marc Maurer, pastor of Journey Church in Grand Junction, Colo. “We are not told how many people really are missing. Flash floods are worse than what we have been told in the news.

“What is being reported is what is easily accessible,” the Nepali pastor continued. “The damage is more far-reaching than that.”

Reports from partners on the ground working with Southern Baptists’ global humanitarian and community ministry Send Relief underscored the severity of the situation, with aid efforts complicated by worsening road conditions and monsoon rains.

Maurer has been serving in short-term missions in Nepal since 2011. He leads pastoral training sessions over a two-week period each fall throughout Nepal at numerous sites.

He is familiar with the terrain left devastated when a slab of ice 49 acres in size (equal to 37 American football fields) broke off a glacier in the Himalayans Aug. 26.

A cascading wall of melted ice, pulverized rock and mud fell 10,000 feet in 50 minutes through narrow mountain gorges on its way down to the plains. The sludge that reached as high as 250 feet on the sides of the gorges swallowed homes, villages and towns of four to six story buildings that had clung to either side of the Bhotekoshi river system, which meanders along the Nepal/China border.

Various news media, including the onsite reporting of India Today , told of 41 bridges and a dozen hydro plants severely damaged or destroyed, 25 miles of road obliterated, and 20 schools gone in an area of about 93,000 people.

“More than 20 pastors and 200 Christian families are missing,” the Nepali pastor texted Maurer on Aug. 28.

Maurer told Baptist Press he personally knows pastors who are working with a network of other pastors in the region.

“What’s amazing to see,” Maurer said, “is that as these pastors meet physical needs with the help of donations from partner churches in America, they share the Gospel and people who have lost everything get the hope they need to start over, this time with Jesus at their side.”

Maurer knows devastation. He was by God’s providence onsite in 2015 when a 7.8 earthquake in central Nepal resulted in nearly 9,000 deaths and massive destruction. Maurer and his team of five Colorado pastors were on a short-term mission to train network leaders when the earthquake hit.

Restricted travel left them stranded in Kathmandu, where they pivoted and ministered to those displaced by the quake, handing out hundreds of New Testaments written in the Nepali language, praying with the displaced victims, and sharing the gospel message.

“We saw several come to Christ,” Maurer said. The Colorado pastor’s background as an architect became useful as he worked with Southern Baptists, providing building inspections for the housing of displaced international and local ministry partners.

“Southern Baptists distributed tons of supplies and hundreds of people came to know the Lord,” Maurer said as a result of Western Colorado churches in 2015 raising much-needed relief funds. “The funds from Western Colorado helped to purchase tarps for temporary shelters, potable water, and food supplies. Partnering with Nepali Network pastors and local government officials, the distribution of these supplies was safeguarded and met the needs of more than 2,000 people in some of the hardest-hit areas.

“Prayer, Bible distribution, and the faithful presentation of the Gospel message by these network pastors and their churches resulted in multitudes of professions of faith, baptisms, and the planting of numerous new churches,” Maurer added.

The difference between the 2015 earthquake and the Aug. 26 glacier-fall is the difference between rubble and mud the texture of wet concrete, he said.

“This time flooding left mounds of sand and mud and debris in and around peoples’ homes,” Maurer said. “Downstream towns, including Galchhi, were flooded in mud up to six feet. For the survivors of that, there’s the difficulty of finding food and especially water. Flooding always destroys wells and other potable water sources.”

The southern half of Nepal, called the Terai Region, is wide river valleys and plains, where a wide range of crops grow. “Certain areas will grow rice, others, beans, and in a lot of these places, crops are grown for a regional distribution,” Maurer said. “So, if crops are destroyed, they affect a vast number of people.”

Southern Baptist Send Relief has been onsite in Nepal since Aug. 27 working with local partners in Nepal to distribute emergency supplies and aid within 24 hours of the disaster, including food staples, first aid and hygiene kits, water filters and purification tablets, cookware, blankets, tarps and tents, mosquito nets and solar lights.

“Send Relief works through local partners and believers who are already in these communities to assess what each village needs,” said a Send Relief leader of a Disaster Assistance Response Team, whose identity was withheld due to security concerns. “We help them identify the full range of needs in their communities – clean water, sanitation, food, shelter, healthcare, and the emotional weight families are carrying – and then equip them to meet those needs.

“Our prayer is that as we serve alongside these communities, everyone will have the opportunity to hear the hope of the Gospel.”

Since Send Relief’s Nepal flood response began, the organization has distributed aid through partners and believers on the ground to more than 3,000 survivors of the disaster.

“The churches we work with are already there and will still be there long after the water is gone,” said Jason Cox, Send Relief’s vice president for international ministry.

“Families in Nepal are still waiting for answers,” he said. “Please pray for families grieving the loss of loved ones, for those searching while waiting for word, for families who lost their homes, for rescue workers moving through dangerous conditions, and for the churches and believers in Nepal serving their neighbors, that they would bring real comfort to their friends and neighbors as they share the hope of Jesus.”

Donations can be made online at SendRelief.org.

Send Relief shared video of a pastor in Nepal thanking the organization and its supporters for the much-needed aid.

“Our efforts during the 2015 earthquake helped me to see firsthand how Southern Baptists managed relief funding at scale, where the funds given were the funds distributed in the field, in the hardest-hit locations,” Maurer said. “This year our spearhead efforts will work through Send Relief with similar anticipated results for the victims of this natural disaster.”

ग्रांड जंक्शन, कोलोराडो (बी.पी.) – काठमांडू केरऽ एगो अनाम ईसाई चर्च केरऽ पादरी आरू पूरा नेपाल केरऽ पांच सौ स॑ भी अधिक चर्चऽ के नेपाली नेटवर्क केरऽ नेता न॑ कहलकै कि नेपाल केरऽ स्थिति समाचार रिपोर्टऽ स॑ बहुत अधिक भयावह छै ।

नेपाली पादरी ५ सितम्बर क॑ कोलोराडो केरऽ ग्रांड जंक्शन केरऽ जर्नी चर्च केरऽ पादरी मार्क मौरर क॑ मैसेज करी क॑ कहलकै कि प्रत्यक्षदर्शी बताबै छै कि २५ स॑ ३० हजार स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै लेकिन सरकार न॑ मात्र १२,५०० के रिपोर्ट देल॑ छै ।

नेपाली पादरी आगू कहलनि जे, जे रिपोर्ट भ रहल अछि ओ अछि जे आसानी सं सुलभ अछि। “क्षति ओहिसँ बेसी दूरगामी अछि।”

दक्षिणी बैपटिस्ट केरऽ वैश्विक मानवीय आरू सामुदायिक मंत्रालय सेंड रिलीफ के साथ काम करै वाला जमीनी भागीदारऽ के रिपोर्ट न॑ स्थिति के गंभीरता प॑ जोर देल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ सड़कऽ के खराब हालत आरू मानसून के बारिश के वजह स॑ सहायता के प्रयास जटिल होय गेलऽ छै ।

मौरेर 2011 स॑ नेपाल म॑ अल्पकालिक मिशन म॑ सेवा द॑ रहलऽ छै ।हुनी हर गिरावट म॑ पूरा नेपाल म॑ अनेक स्थल प॑ दू सप्ताह के अवधि म॑ पशुपालन प्रशिक्षण सत्र के नेतृत्व करै छै ।

26 अगस्त क॑ हिमालय केरऽ एगो ग्लेशियर क॑ तोड़ी क॑ 49 एकड़ आकार केरऽ बर्फ केरऽ स्लैब (37 अमेरिकी फुटबॉल मैदान के बराबर) जब॑ तबाह होय गेलऽ इलाका स॑ परिचित छै ।

पिघलल बर्फ, चूर्णित चट्टान आ थाल केर झरना सन देबाल मैदान दिस उतरैत काल संकीर्ण पहाड़ी गॉर्ज सं 50 मिनट में 10,000 फीट खसि पड़ल. गॉर्ज के कात में 250 फीट तक ऊँच कीचड़ नेपाल/चीन सीमा पर घुमावदार भोटेकोशी नदी प्रणाली के दुनू कात चिपकल चारि सं छह मंजिला भवन के घर, गाम आ शहर के निगल गेल छल.

इंडिया टुडे केरऽ ऑनसाइट रिपोर्टिंग सहित विभिन्न न्यूज मीडिया न॑ लगभग ९३,००० लोगऽ के इलाका म॑ ४१ पुल आरू एक दर्जन हाइड्रो प्लांट क॑ गंभीर रूप स॑ क्षतिग्रस्त या नष्ट होय गेलऽ, २५ मील के सड़क मिटाबै के बारे म॑ बतैलकै ।

नेपाली पादरी 28 अगस्त कए मौरर कए मेसेज केलथि जे, 20 स बेसी पास्टर आ 200 ईसाई परिवार लापता अछि।

मौरर न॑ बैपटिस्ट प्रेस क॑ बतैलकै कि हुनी व्यक्तिगत रूप स॑ वू पास्टर क॑ जान॑ छै जे क्षेत्र केरऽ अन्य पादरी केरऽ नेटवर्क के साथ काम करी रहलऽ छै ।

मौरर कहलकै, “जे देखना आश्चर्यजनक छै, वू ई छै कि जेना-जेना ई पास्टर अमेरिका केरऽ पार्टनर चर्चऽ के दान के मदद स॑ शारीरिक जरूरतऽ क॑ पूरा करै छै, वू सुसमाचार क॑ साझा करै छै आरू जे लोगऽ क॑ सब कुछ गंवाय देलऽ गेलऽ छै, ओकरा वू आशा मिलै छै कि ओकरा नया सिरा स॑ शुरू करै के जरूरत छै, ई बार यीशु के साथ ।

मौरेर तबाही जनैत अछि। ओ 2015 मे भगवान के प्रोविडेंस स ऑनसाइट छलाह जखन मध्य नेपाल मे 7.8 के भूकंप आयल छल जाहि मे लगभग 9000 लोक के मौत भ गेल छल आ भारी तबाही भेल छल. मौरर आरू हुनकऽ पांच कोलोराडो पादरी के टीम नेटवर्क केरऽ नेता सिनी क॑ प्रशिक्षित करै के अल्पकालिक मिशन प॑ छेलै जब॑ भूकंप आबी गेलै ।

प्रतिबंधित यात्रा के कारण काठमांडू में फंसल रहलै, जहां भूकंप के कारण विस्थापित लोगऽ के पिवट करी क॑ सेवा करलकै, नेपाली भाषा में लिखलऽ सैकड़ों नया नियम बाँटलकै, विस्थापित पीड़ितऽ के साथ प्रार्थना करलकै, आरू सुसमाचार के संदेश साझा करलकै ।

मौरर कहलनि जे, हम कतेको गोटे के मसीह लग आयल देखलहुं। कोलोराडो केरऽ पादरी केरऽ पृष्ठभूमि एक आर्किटेक्ट के रूप म॑ उपयोगी होय गेलै, कैन्हेंकि हुनी दक्षिणी बैपटिस्ट के साथ काम करलकै, विस्थापित अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आरू स्थानीय मंत्रालय भागीदारऽ के आवास लेली भवन निरीक्षण प्रदान करलकै ।

2015 म॑ पश्चिमी कोलोराडो चर्चऽ न॑ बहुत जरूरी राहत धन जुटाबै के परिणामस्वरूप मौरर न॑ कहलकै कि दक्षिणी बैपटिस्ट न॑ टन आपूर्ति बांटलकै आरू सैकड़ों लोग प्रभु क॑ जान॑ लगलै । “पश्चिमी कोलोराडो केरऽ फंड स॑ अस्थायी आश्रय, पीबै वाला पानी, आरू खाद्य आपूर्ति लेली टारप खरीदै म॑ मदद मिललै । नेपाली नेटवर्क केरऽ पादरी आरू स्थानीय सरकार केरऽ अधिकारी सिनी के साथ साझेदारी करी क॑ ई आपूर्ति के वितरण के सुरक्षा करलऽ गेलै आरू कुछ सबसें प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ २००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के जरूरत पूरा करलऽ गेलै ।

मौरर न॑ आरू कहलकै, “प्रार्थना, बाइबिल वितरण, आरू ई नेटवर्क पादरी आरू ओकरऽ कलीसिया द्वारा सुसमाचार के संदेश के निष्ठापूर्वक प्रस्तुति के परिणामस्वरूप विश्वास केरऽ कई तरह के पेशे, बपतिस्मा आरू अनेक नया कलीसिया के रोपनी पैदा होय गेलै ।

ओ कहला जे 2015 क भूकंप आ 26 अगस्त कए ग्लेशियर-फॉल क अंतर मलबा आ गीला कंक्रीट क बनावट मे कीचड़ क अंतर अछि।

मौरर कहलनि जे, एहि बेर बाढ़ि सं लोकक घर आ ओकर आसपास बालु आ थाल आ मलबा के टीला भ गेल। “गलछी सहित डाउनस्ट्रीम शहर छह फीट धरि थाल मे बाढ़ि मे आबि गेल छल. ओहि मे सँ बचि गेल लोक लेल भोजन आ खास क’ पानि भेटबा मे दिक्कत होइत छैक. बाढ़ि मे सदिखन इनार आ अन्य पीबय योग्य पानिक स्रोत नष्ट भ’ जाइत छैक.”

नेपाल के दक्षिणी आधा भाग जेकरा तराई क्षेत्र कहलऽ जाय छै, चौड़ा नदी घाटी आरू मैदान छै, जहां विस्तृत श्रृंखला के फसल उपजै छै । मौरर कहला जे किछु खास इलाका मे धान, दोसर, बीन्स क खेती होएत, आ एहि मे स बहुत ठाम क्षेत्रीय वितरण लेल फसल क खेती कैल जाइत अछि। “त, जँ फसल नष्ट भ’ जायत त’ एकर असर विशाल संख्या मे लोक पर पड़ैत छैक।”

दक्षिणी बैपटिस्ट सेंड रिलीफ नेपाल मे 1 अगस्त स ऑनसाइट अछि। 27 नेपाल मे स्थानीय साझेदारक संग मिलिकय आपदाक 24 घंटाक भीतर आपातकालीन आपूर्ति आ सहायता वितरित करय, जाहि मे खाद्य पदार्थ, प्राथमिक चिकित्सा आ स्वच्छता किट, जल छानय वाला आ शुद्धिकरण गोली, खाना बनाबय वाला बर्तन, कम्बल, टारप आ टेंट, मच्छरदानी आ सौर रोशनी शामिल अछि.

एकटा आपदा सहायता प्रतिक्रिया टीम केरऽ सेंड रिलीफ नेता न॑ कहलकै, “सेंड रिलीफ स्थानीय भागीदार आरू विश्वासी के माध्यम स॑ काम करै छै जे पहल॑ स॑ ही ई समुदायऽ म॑ छै आरू ई आकलन करै छै कि हर गाँव क॑ की जरूरत छै । “हम ओकरा अपन समुदाय मे जरूरतक कें पूरा श्रृंखला कें पहचान करय मे मदद करय छी – स्वच्छ पानी, स्वच्छता, भोजन, आवास, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल, आ भावनात्मक वजन जे परिवारक कें उठाएल जा रहल छै – आ ओकर बाद ओकरा ओय जरूरतक कें पूरा करय कें लेल सुसज्जित करय छै.

“हमरऽ प्रार्थना छै कि जैन्हऽ-जैन्हऽ हम्में ई समुदायऽ के साथ-साथ सेवा करबै, सब क॑ सुसमाचार के आशा सुनै के मौका मिलतै।”

जहिया स सेंड रिलीफ के नेपाल बाढ़िक प्रतिक्रिया शुरू भेल अछि तहिया स संस्था एहि आपदा स बचि गेल तीन हजार स बेसी लोक कए जमीन पर साझेदार आ आस्तिक क माध्यम स सहायता वितरित केलक अछि।

सेंड रिलीफ केरऽ अंतरराष्ट्रीय मंत्रालय केरऽ उपाध्यक्ष जेसन कॉक्स न॑ कहलकै कि जे चर्च के साथ हम्मं॑ काम करै छियै, वू पहिने स॑ ही छै आरू पानी खतम होय के बहुत बाद भी वहीं रहतै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे परिवार एखनो जवाबक प्रतीक्षा मे अछि। “कृपया अपन प्रियजन के क्षति के शोक संतप्त परिवार के लेल, शब्द के इंतजार में खोज करय वाला परिवार के लेल, अपन घर गंवा चुकल परिवार के लेल, खतरनाक परिस्थिति में आगू बढ़य वाला बचावकर्मी के लेल, आ नेपाल में अपन पड़ोसी के सेवा करय वाला चर्च आ विश्वासी के लेल प्रार्थना करू जे ओ सब अपन मित्र आ पड़ोसी के लेल वास्तविक आराम आनय जेना ओ यीशु के आशा के साझा करैत छथि।”

दान SendRelief.org पर ऑनलाइन देल जा सकैत अछि।

नेपाल के एकटा पादरी के बहुत जरूरी सहायता के लेल संस्था आ ओकर समर्थक के धन्यवाद दैत सेंड रिलीफ शेयर केल गेल वीडियो।

मौरर न॑ कहलकै कि २०१५ केरऽ भूकंप के दौरान हमरऽ प्रयास न॑ हमरा खुद देखै म॑ मदद करलकै कि दक्षिणी बैपटिस्ट न॑ कोना पैमाना प॑ राहत केरऽ फंडिंग के प्रबंधन करलकै, जहां देलऽ गेलऽ फंड मैदान म॑ वितरित करलऽ गेलऽ फंड छेलै, सबस॑ बेसी प्रभावित स्थानऽ प॑ । “ई साल हमरऽ अग्रणी प्रयास सेंड रिलीफ के माध्यम स॑ काम करतै जेकरा म॑ ई प्राकृतिक आपदा के शिकार लोगऽ लेली भी ऐसनऽ ही प्रत्याशित परिणाम मिलतै।”

title: An ocean away from Nepal, Sonia spends her spare time piecing together clues about missing flood victims: ‘I wanted to be useful’ - The Guardian
description: An ocean away from Nepal, Sonia spends her spare time piecing together clues about missing flood victims: ‘I wanted to be useful’  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
A chain of flowers tattooed from knee to foot, a gold nose ring worn on a left nostril, a primary school tie caked in mud: these are the images that linger in Sonia Patil’s mind as she tries to help Nepali flood victims find their loved ones.

More than 1,300 have died and at least 5,500 have been reported missing since a glacial collapse sent a torrent of water, mud, ice and debris through riverside communities along the Nepal-Tibet border on 26 August.

Families and friends of those reported missing have spent weeks searching through graphic photos of bodies, which were uploaded by Nepali police for the community to identify.

Who are the Australians missing in the Nepal floods? What we know so far Read more

Some show only partial corpses – disconnected torsos, limbs splayed at unnatural angles, decomposition eating away at extremities – while in others, the faces of flood victims are turned to the camera, their expressions frozen in their death masks.

Patil, a Melbourne-based chef, has no direct connection with Nepal or any of the people whose loved ones have been reported missing. But when she saw videos of their grief, she knew she could help share their burden.

“It’s a very harrowing task for them,” she says.

“If I had lost a family member, the prospect of coming across their body in that condition would be unbearable.

“I knew I wanted to be useful, it’s the least I can do, even if it’s just being another pair of eyes.”

View image in fullscreen A portion of Patil’s list describing distinguishing features found in pictures of unidentified victims of the Nepali floods. Illustration: Sonia Patil

Almost every day since the disaster, she arrives home at midnight after a 12-hour shift and spends another four to five hours on the Nepali police website, trawling through the hundreds of images of decomposing bodies and limbs.

If any have distinctive features - like clothes, tattoos and jewellery – she adds them to her list and posts it to Facebook groups filled with those looking for their loved ones.

It can be a confronting and tedious process, Patil says.

During the day, the Nepal police website slows or malfunctions under the weight of all the families looking for information, so she finds it easier to work at night.

The listings, which grow by the day, may only show partial remains, and most only have one image per body – meaning she cannot see any other angles.

Missing persons posters are also spread across multiple platforms, forcing Patil to search across the internet to crosscheck information.

View image in fullscreen When members think they have made a match, the group asks relatives to submit their DNA to labs in Nepal for official confirmation. Photograph: Monika Malla/Reuters

But no matter how hard it is, she says it is worse for those on the ground.

“It’s very disturbing to know that I may be looking at a picture of a live person and somebody who is deceased at the same time, trying to compare them,” she says.

“I find it easier when I go in with the mindset that all the images on that website are all human: they have lived lives, they have stories, they have families looking for them.”

As Nepal’s morgues fill, Parkrit hopes her DNA can be used to find her mother Read more

Patil is part of a group which includes people from the US, Europe, New Zealand and other countries who work together to identify bodies. They generally look for matches for those who have reached out to them with photos of their missing friends and family.

It is difficult to be 100% certain through visual identification alone, as many images of the bodies are unrecognisable. So when members think they have made a match, the group asks relatives to submit their DNA to labs in Nepal for official confirmation.

If they believe they have made a match for someone who has not asked for their help, the group tries to report it to Nepali authorities.

Making a likely identification is bittersweet for everyone involved, Patil says, because while they are glad a family will get closure, “it’s not a great feeling to know that person is no longer here”.

But it is worse when she posts her lists and no one responds.

View image in fullscreen ‘So long as I can find tattoos or anything identifiable, I will keep going,’ Patil says. Photograph: Penny Stephens/The Guardian

“In some cases, entire families have been wiped out, which means that even people with the most recognisable tattoos have nobody left to identify them,” she says.

Patil does not want any thanks for her work. Instead, she urges everyone to keep sharing the lists in case someone in their network recognises the missing.

It is now becoming harder to discern any distinctive features as the bodies disintegrate under the sun and sludge with the passing days. But Patil has vowed to continue.

“So long as I can find tattoos or anything identifiable, I will keep going,” she says.

मेलबर्न के शेफ पाटिल के नेपाल या कोनो एहन लोक सं सीधा संबंध नहिं अछि जिनकर प्रियजन के लापता होय के खबर अछि. मुदा जखन हुनकर दुखक वीडियो देखलनि त हुनका बुझल छलनि जे ओ हुनकर बोझ बांटय मे मदद क सकैत छथि।

ओ कहैत छथि, “हुनका लेल ई बहुत दुखद काज अछि.”

ओ कहला जे अगर हम परिवार क कोनो सदस्य कए गंवा देने रहितहुं त ओहि हालत मे हुनकर शरीर स भेंट करबाक संभावना असहनीय रहैत।

“हमरा बुझल छल जे हम उपयोगी बन’ चाहैत छी, ई हमरा सँ कम सँ कम काज अछि, भले ई मात्र एकटा आओर आँखिक जोड़ी बनब हो.”

फुलस्क्रीन मे छवि देखू पाटिल के सूची के एकटा हिस्सा जाहि मे नेपाली बाढ़ि के अज्ञात पीड़ित के तस्वीर मे भेटल विशिष्ट विशेषता के वर्णन अछि. चित्रण : सोनिया पाटिल

अगर कोनो में विशिष्ट विशेषता छै - जेना कपड़ा, गोदना आ गहना - त ओ ओकरा अपन सूची में जोड़ि क फेसबुक ग्रुप में पोस्ट क दैत छथि जे अपन प्रियजन के खोजय वाला लोक सं भरल रहैत अछि.

पाटिल कहैत छथि जे इ एकटा सामना आ थकाऊ प्रक्रिया भ सकैत अछि।

दिन मे नेपाल पुलिसक वेबसाइट सूचना ताकय बला सभ परिवारक भार सँ धीमा भ' जाइत छैक वा खराब भ' जाइत छैक, तेँ ओकरा राति मे काज करब सहज बुझाइत छैक ।

दिन पर बढ़ैत लिस्टिंग मे आंशिक अवशेष मात्र देखा सकैत अछि, आ बेसी मे प्रति शरीर मात्र एकटा छवि होइत छैक – मतलब जे ओ कोनो आन कोण नहि देखि सकैत छथि ।

लापता लोगऽ के पोस्टर भी कई प्लेटफार्मऽ प॑ फैललऽ छै, जेकरा चलतें पाटिल क॑ जानकारी के क्रॉसचेक करै लेली पूरा इंटरनेट प॑ खोज करै ल॑ पड़ै छै ।

View image in fullscreen जखन सदस्य सब के लगैत छैक जे हम सब मिलान केने छी त समूह रिश्तेदार सब स कहैत अछि जे आधिकारिक पुष्टि के लेल नेपाल के लैब में अपन डीएनए जमा करू। फोटोग्राफ : मोनिका मल्ला/रायटर

मुदा कतबो कठिन किएक नहि हो मुदा ओ कहैत छथि जे जमीन पर बैसल लोक लेल इ बेसी खराब अछि।

ओ कहैत छथि, “ई जानि क’ बहुत परेशानी होइत अछि जे हम एकहि संग कोनो जीवित व्यक्ति आ कियो मृतकक तस्वीर देखैत भ’ सकैत छी, ओकर तुलना करबाक प्रयास मे भ’ सकैत छी.”

“हमरा तखन ई मानसिकताक संग भीतर जाइत छी जे ओहि वेबसाइट पर जतेक छवि अछि से सबटा मनुक्खक अछि: ओ सभ जीवन जीने छथि, हुनका सभक कथा छनि, हुनका सभक परिवार छनि जे ओकरा खोजैत छथि।”

जेना-जेना नेपाल के मुर्दाघर भरैत अछि, पर्रित के उम्मीद अछि जे हुनकर डीएनए के इस्तेमाल सं हुनकर मां के खोजल जा सकैत अछि आओर पढ़ू

पाटिल एकटा समूह के हिस्सा छै जेकरा म॑ अमेरिका, यूरोप, न्यूजीलैंड आरू अन्य देशऽ के लोग शामिल छै जे मिल क॑ लाश के पहचान करै छै । आम तौर पर ओ सब ओहि लोकनिक लेल मैच तकैत छथि जे अपन लापता मित्र आ परिवारक फोटो ल' क' हुनका सभ सं संपर्क केने छथि.

केवल दृश्य पहचान के माध्यम स शत-प्रतिशत निश्चित होयब मुश्किल अछि, कियाक त लाश के बहुत रास छवि चिन्हल नै जा सकैत अछि । अतः जखन सदस्य सब के लगैत छनि जे हम सब मिलान केने छी त समूह रिश्तेदार सब स कहैत अछि जे आधिकारिक पुष्टि के लेल अपन डीएनए नेपाल के लैब में जमा करू।

यदि हुनका विश्वास छै कि जे कियो मदद नै मँगने छै ओकरा लेली मैच बनैने छै त॑ समूह नेपाली अधिकारियऽ क॑ रिपोर्ट करै के कोशिश करै छै ।

पाटिल कहैत छथि जे संभावित पहचान करब एहि मे शामिल सब गोटे लेल मीठ-मीठ अछि, कारण जखन कि हुनका खुशी अछि जे कोनो परिवार कए बंदी भेटत, “ई जानब कोनो पैघ एहसास नहि अछि जे ओ व्यक्ति आब एतय नहि अछि”।

मुदा तखन आओर खराब भ जाएत अछि जखन ओ अपन लिस्ट पोस्ट करैत छथिन्ह आओर कियो कोनो जवाब नहि दैत छथिन्ह.

फुलस्क्रीन मे छवि देखू ‘जा धरि हमरा गोदना या कोनो पहचान योग्य चीज भेटत, हम आगू बढ़ैत रहब,’ पाटिल कहैत छथि। फोटोग्राफ : पेनी स्टीफंस/द गार्जियन

ओ कहैत छथि जे किछु मामला मे पूरा परिवार कए सफाया करि देल गेल अछि, मतलब जे सबस चिन्हल-जानल टैटू वाला लोक कए सेहो हुनकर पहचान करबा लेल कियो नहि बचल अछि।

पाटिल अपन काज लेल कोनो धन्यवाद नहि चाहैत छथि। बल्कि ओ सब गोटे स आग्रह करैत छथि जे एहि लिस्ट कए शेयर करैत रहू जाहि स हुनकर नेटवर्क मे कियो लापता कए चिन्हि लेत।

आब कोनो विशिष्ट विशेषताक भेद करब कठिन भ' रहल अछि, कारण बीतैत दिनक संग शरीर सभ रौदक नीचाँ विघटित भ' रहल अछि आ कीचड़ भ' रहल अछि. मुदा पाटिल आगू बढ़बाक प्रण केने छथि।

ओ कहैत छथि जे जा धरि हमरा गोदना या कोनो पहचान योग्य चीज भेटत ता धरि हम आगू बढ़ैत रहब।

description: Doctor who recently graduated University of Minnesota fellowship among those missing in Nepal  CBS News

full_article:
A doctor with ties to the University of Minnesota and his family have been declared missing in the wake of the devastating Nepal flash floods.

On Tuesday, the university's Department of Orthopedic Surgery announced "with deep sadness" that Dr. Ishan Patel, a recent graduate of the Adult Reconstructive Fellowship, traveled to Nepal with his wife, mother and father-in-law.

The university says Patel and his family were likely at their hotel when the flooding occurred. The hotel was swept away, and Patel and his family are currently declared missing.

"This situation continues to evolve, and recovery efforts in the region are ongoing. Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with Dr. Patel, his family, and all those affected by this tragedy," the university said in a statement.

Patel was in Nepal on a pilgrimage after his graduation.

At least 1,300 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, which were likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal's disaster management agency. Dozens of Americans are among the missing.

title: See Nepalese rescue workers provide disaster relief via drone - CBC
description: See Nepalese rescue workers provide disaster relief via drone  CBC
publisher.title: CBC
full_article:
With roads and bridges destroyed and helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last month's devastating floods, Nepal's army is turning to drones to ‌deliver relief to displaced people.

At least 1,367 people are confirmed dead and more than 5,000 are missing in Nepal since a Himalayan glacier broke off near the ​Nepal-China border in late August and ​caused devastation along rivers farther downstream.

A DJI FlyCart 100 drone carrying relief goods flies during an aid delivery mission to stranded residents hit by deadly flash floods and mudslides in Devighat, Nepal, on Sept. 8. (Joseph Campbell/Reuters)

"Most of our helicopters are busy with rescue operations. There is no other way ​to send food, essentials, medicine and fuel, except for ⁠drones, which are ⁠the best option to ‌utilize, and we should prioritize them more," said Santosh Budhathoki, a contract drone pilot for the Nepal army.

Drones are used over distances of three to four ⁠kilometres and can haul up to 60 kilograms at a time. They are already making an impact for ‌affected communities in dire need of aid, Budhathoki said.

A drone carrying relief supplies to a flood-affected area is seen in Trishuli, Nepal, on Sept. 4. (Prabin Ranabhat/AFP/Getty Images)

The army is now making around 10 to 16 aid deliveries a day with a fleet of four DJI FlyCart 100 drones, all ​donated from China as part of a recent aid package.

In addition to aid delivery, ⁠drones have also been used to move the bodies of flood ⁠victims in some affected areas, while reconnaissance drones have also ⁠been ⁠heavily used in search ​and rescue operations.

A drone pilot uses his gear during an interview in Trishuli, Nepal, on Sept. 7. (Pedro Pardo/AFP/Getty Images)

"We’ve been operating back and forth early in the morning. So ​yes, it is ⁠quite hectic, because we need to have this thing right now," said Milan Pandey, of the drone-operating company Airlift Technology.

"Nepal has this geography, this terrain where drones would be really faster, quicker and cheaper," ⁠Pandey said.

नेपाल केरऽ देवीघाट म॑ ८ सितम्बर क॑ जानलेवा आकस्मिक बाढ़ आरू कीचड़ गिरला स॑ फंसलऽ निवासी सिनी क॑ सहायता पहुँचै के अभियान के दौरान राहत सामान ले जाय वाला डीजीआई फ्लाईकार्ट १०० ड्रोन उड़ै छै ।(जोसेफ कैम्पबेल/रायटर)

नेपाली सेना केरऽ ठेका ड्रोन पायलट संतोष बुधाथोकी नँ कहलकै, "हमरऽ अधिकांश हेलीकॉप्टर बचाव अभियान मँ व्यस्त छै । भोजन, आवश्यक सामान, दवाई आरू ईंधन भेजै के दोसरऽ तरीका नै छै, सिवाय ⁠ड्रोन के, जेकरऽ उपयोग करै लेली ⁠सबसे अच्छा विकल्प छै, आरू हमरा सब क॑ ओकरा अधिक प्राथमिकता देना चाहियऽ ।

ड्रोन केरऽ उपयोग तीन स॑ चार ⁠किलोमीटर के दूरी प॑ करलऽ जाय छै आरू एक बार म॑ ६० किलोग्राम तलक के पानी खींच॑ सकै छै । बुधाथोकी कहलनि जे, ओ सब पहिने सं सहायता के सख्त जरूरत वाला प्रभावित समुदाय के लेल प्रभाव डाल रहल अछि।

बाढ़ प्रभावित इलाका मे राहत सामान ल जा रहल ड्रोन 4 सितम्बर कए नेपाल क त्रिशुली मे देखल जा रहल अछि।(प्रबीन रानाभाट/एएफपी/गेटी इमेजेज)

सेना अब॑ चारि डीजीआई फ्लाईकार्ट १०० ड्रोन के बेड़ा के साथ रोजाना लगभग १० स॑ १६ सहायता डिलीवरी करी रहलऽ छै, जे सब चीन स॑ हाल केरऽ सहायता पैकेज के तहत दान करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

सहायता पहुँचै के अलावा, ⁠ड्रोन के उपयोग कुछ प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ में बाढ़ ⁠पीड़ितऽ के लाश क॑ ले जाय लेली भी करलऽ गेलऽ छै, जबकि टोही ड्रोन के इस्तेमाल भी ⁠खोज आरू बचाव अभियान म॑ ⁠बहुत करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

7 सितम्बर के नेपाल के त्रिशुली में साक्षात्कार के दौरान ड्रोन पायलट अपन गियर के उपयोग करैत अछि।(पेड्रो पारदो/एएफपी/गेटी इमेजेज)

ड्रोन संचालित कंपनी एयरलिफ्ट टेक्नोलॉजी के मिलन पांडेय कहलनि जे, हम सब भोरे-भोर आगू-पाछू संचालित करैत रहलहुं अछि.त हाँ, ई ⁠काफी व्यस्त अछि, कारण हमरा सब लग एखन ई चीज हेबाक जरूरत अछि।

⁠पाण्डेय कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे ई भूगोल अछि, ई इलाका अछि जतय ड्रोन सचमुच तेज, तेज आ सस्ता होयत।

title: 18 Americans Safe After Nepal Floods, About 70 Still Missing - INDIA New England News
description: 18 Americans Safe After Nepal Floods, About 70 Still Missing  INDIA New England News

full_article:
Washington — Eighteen Americans reported missing after catastrophic floods in Nepal have reached safety, while about 70 remain unaccounted for in the Nepal-China border region, the US State Department said Tuesday.

The updated figures were provided as of 7 a.m. Eastern Time on September 8, according to a State Department spokesperson.

The department said it remains in close contact with the families of Americans still missing and is committed to providing regular updates as more information becomes available.

“We extend our deepest sympathy to all those affected by the flooding in Nepal, and their families, and we reaffirm our enduring friendship with the Nepali people,” the spokesperson said.

The State Department warned Americans outside the affected region against traveling there for any reason, citing continued risks from flash floods and landslides.

The update came after Indian-American Representatives Raja Krishnamoorthi, Ro Khanna and Suhas Subramanyam joined 27 members of Congress in urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to strengthen the US response.

The lawmakers asked the State Department to deploy specialized disaster teams and advanced surveillance assets to help locate thousands of people reported missing after the floods.

“We write to urge the State Department to use every available resource to support ongoing search-and-rescue efforts following the catastrophic flash floods in Nepal and to ensure the safety and recovery of American citizens and others affected by this disaster,” the lawmakers said in a September 4 letter.

The disaster followed an August 26 glacial collapse and landslide in the Himalayas. Water, mud and debris swept through the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi river corridors, devastating communities in Nepal and Gyirong County.

The lawmakers said the floods destroyed roads, bridges, homes and other critical infrastructure. They cited reports that the death toll had surpassed 1,300 and that at least 4,000 people remained missing.

They welcomed $500,000 in State Department assistance through Catholic Relief Services for emergency shelter, relief supplies, and water, sanitation and hygiene assistance. They also acknowledged $3.6 million in US humanitarian aid announced on August 29.

“Nonetheless, given the unprecedented loss of life and countless missing persons, we urge the Department to do much more,” they said.

The lawmakers called for daily updates to families of missing people and to Congress, as well as adequate staffing for consular hotlines and assistance with the repatriation of US citizens and their families.

They also urged the immediate deployment of a Disaster Assistance Response Team, or DART, to support search operations, rescue work, logistics and medical services.

“The scale of the catastrophe requires DART deployment as soon as possible,” the letter said.

The lawmakers asked the department to coordinate with other US agencies and private companies to deploy high-altitude assets and thermal or infrared drones. They also proposed using geospatial and aerial imagery, commercial satellite information and phone location data to help trace missing people.

They urged diplomatic coordination with Nepal, China, donor countries and international organizations to secure access to search areas.

Americans seeking information about relatives can call the State Department toll-free from the US and Canada at 1-888-407-4747. Those calling from other locations can use 1-202-501-4444.

The US Embassy in Beijing can be reached at 010-8531-4000 from China or 011-86-10-8531-4000 from the United States.

India has sent temporary shelters, blankets, medicines and other emergency supplies. Britain, South Korea, China, the United Nations, the World Bank and non-governmental organizations have also announced assistance.

The Indo-American Arts Council said part of the proceeds from every ticket sold for its Erasing Borders Dance Festival at Kaye Playhouse in New York on September 19 and 20 would go to the Nepalese government’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund. (Source: IANS)

वाशिंगटन : नेपाल मँ विनाशकारी बाढ़ के बाद अठारह अमेरिकी के लापता होय के खबर मिललै, जबकि नेपाल-चीन सीमा क्षेत्र मँ लगभग 70 अमेरिकी के बेहिसाब छै ।

विदेश विभाग के प्रवक्ता के अनुसार 8 सितंबर के पूर्वी समय के अनुसार 7 बजे तक अपडेट आंकड़ा उपलब्ध करायल गेल छल।

विभाग नँ कहलकै कि हुनी अखनी तलक लापता अमेरिकी सिनी के परिवारौ के साथ घनिष्ठ संपर्क मँ छै आरू अधिक जानकारी उपलब्ध होय के साथ-साथ नियमित रूप सँ अपडेट दै लेली प्रतिबद्ध छै ।

प्रवक्ता कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे बाढ़ि सं प्रभावित सब गोटे, आ हुनकर परिवार के प्रति हम सब गहींर संवेदना व्यक्त करैत छी, आ नेपाली जनता के संग अपन स्थायी मित्रता के दोबारा पुष्टि करैत छी।

विदेश विभाग न॑ प्रभावित क्षेत्र स॑ बाहर के अमेरिकी लोगऽ क॑ कोनो भी कारण स॑ वहाँ जाय स॑ नै जाय के चेतावनी देल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ झटका बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन स॑ लगातार खतरा के हवाला देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ई अपडेट भारतीय-अमेरिकी प्रतिनिधि राजा कृष्णमूर्ति, रो खन्ना आरू सुहास सुब्रमण्यम न॑ कांग्रेस केरऽ २७ सदस्यऽ के साथ मिल क॑ विदेश सचिव मार्को रूबियो स॑ अमेरिका केरऽ प्रतिक्रिया क॑ मजबूत करै के आग्रह करला के बाद आबी गेलऽ छै ।

विधायक न॑ विदेश विभाग स॑ कहलकै कि बाढ़ के बाद लापता होय के खबर मिललऽ हजारों लोगऽ के पता लगाबै म॑ मदद लेली विशेष आपदा टीम आरू उन्नत निगरानी संपत्ति तैनात करलऽ जाय ।

विधायक सब ४ सितम्बर के पत्र मे कहलनि जे, हम विदेश विभाग स आग्रह करय लेल लिखैत छी जे नेपाल मे विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के बाद जारी खोज आ बचाव प्रयास के समर्थन करय आ अमेरिकी नागरिक आ एहि आपदा स प्रभावित अन्य लोक के सुरक्षा आ बरामदगी सुनिश्चित करय लेल उपलब्ध हर संसाधन के उपयोग करय।

ई आपदा 26 अगस्त क॑ हिमालय केरऽ पतन आरू हिमालय म॑ भूस्खलन के बाद आबी गेलऽ छै । त्रिशुली आ भोटे कोशी नदी गलियारा मे पानि, थाल आ मलबा बहैत नेपाल आ ग्यरोंग काउंटी के समुदाय के तबाह क देलक।

विधायक सब कहलनि जे, बाढ़ि स सड़क, पुल, घर आ अन्य महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढांचा तबाह भ गेल। ओ सब एहि खबर के हवाला देलखिन्ह जे मृतक के संख्या 1300 सं बेसि भ गेल अछि आओर कम सं कम 4000 लोक लापता अछि.

हुनी आपातकालीन आश्रय, राहत आपूर्ति, आरू पानी, स्वच्छता आरू स्वच्छता सहायता लेली कैथोलिक राहत सेवा के माध्यम स॑ विदेश विभाग केरऽ ५ लाख डॉलर के सहायता के स्वागत करलकै । ओ सब 29 अगस्त कए घोषित 36 लाख डॉलर क अमेरिकी मानवीय सहायता कए सेहो स्वीकार केलथि।

ओ सब कहलनि जे, एकर बावजूद जान के अभूतपूर्व नुकसान आ अनगिनत लापता व्यक्ति के देखैत हम विभाग स आग्रह करैत छी जे ओ बहुत किछु आओर काज करय।

विधायक सब लापता लोगऽ के परिवार आरू कांग्रेस क॑ रोजाना अपडेट दै के साथ-साथ कांसुलर हॉटलाइन लेली पर्याप्त कर्मचारी आरू अमेरिकी नागरिक आरू ओकरऽ परिवार क॑ वापसी म॑ सहायता के आह्वान करलकै ।

हुनी खोज अभियान, बचाव कार्य, रसद आरू चिकित्सा सेवा मँ सहायता लेली आपदा सहायता प्रतिक्रिया टीम यानी डार्ट क तुरंत तैनाती करै के आग्रह भी करलकै ।

पत्र मे कहल गेल अछि जे, प्रलय क पैमाना पर जल्द स जल्द डार्ट क तैनाती क जरूरत अछि।

विधायक न॑ विभाग स॑ कहलकै कि वू अन्य अमेरिकी एजेंसी आरू निजी कंपनी सिनी के साथ समन्वय करी क॑ उच्च ऊंचाई प॑ पहुँचै वाला संपत्ति आरू थर्मल या इन्फ्रारेड ड्रोन क॑ तैनात करै । हुनी भू-स्थानिक आरू हवाई इमेजरी, वाणिज्यिक उपग्रह जानकारी आरू फोन केरऽ स्थान के आंकड़ा के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ लापता लोगऽ के पता लगाबै म॑ मदद करै के प्रस्ताव भी रखलकै ।

ओ सभ नेपाल, चीन, दाता देश आ अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय संस्था सभक संग कूटनीतिक समन्वय करबाक आग्रह कएलनि जाहिसँ खोज क्षेत्रमे प्रवेश सुरक्षित कएल जा सकए ।

रिश्तेदारक कें बारे मे जानकारी चाहय वाला अमेरिकी अमेरिका आ कनाडा सं विदेश विभाग कें टोल फ्री नंबर 1-888-407-4747 पर फोन कयर सकय छै. जे कियो दोसर स्थान सं फोन क रहल छथिन्ह ओ 1-202-501-4444 के इस्तेमाल क सकय छथिन्ह.

बीजिंग स्थित अमेरिकी दूतावास चीन सं 010-8531-4000 या अमेरिका सं 011-86-10-8531-4000 पर संपर्क कएल जा सकैत अछि.

भारत न॑ अस्थायी आश्रय स्थल, कंबल, दवाई आरू अन्य आपातकालीन सामान भेजलकै । ब्रिटेन, दक्षिण कोरिया, चीन, संयुक्त राष्ट्र, विश्व बैंक आ गैर सरकारी संगठन सेहो मदद के घोषणा केलक अछि।

भारत-अमेरिकन कला परिषद न॑ कहलकै कि १९ आरू २० सितंबर क॑ न्यूयॉर्क केरऽ काये प्लेहाउस म॑ अपनऽ इरेजिंग बॉर्डर्स डांस फेस्टिवल लेली बिकलऽ हर टिकट स॑ मिलै वाला आमदनी के कुछ हिस्सा नेपाल सरकार केरऽ प्रधानमंत्री आपदा राहत कोष म॑ जाय वाला छै । (स्रोत: आईएएनएस)

full_article:
Nepal's search and rescue operation was still underway, when the country was hit by an earthquake on September 8. The casualties from the glacier outburst, that took place on August 26, is increasing every day. The latest government update puts the death count at 1,367, with more than 5,100 people missing. So far, 13,646 people have been rescued, while 7,151 are receiving treatment. More than 21,000 security personnel have been deployed for the response.

The floods followed a collapse in the Himalayan region that sent a large volume of water, mud and debris into the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors.

Countries Step In

Nepal has received help from several countries as its own rescue teams continue to work across the affected areas. India, China and South Korea have provided specialised rescue and forensic support, while countries including the UAE, Japan, Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, the UK and US have sent money, relief material, equipment or technical assistance.

India has sent about 95 tonnes of relief material and 54 personnel, including tunnel-rescue experts, forensic specialists and medical personnel. Indian teams are also helping Nepal with DNA identification and tunnel rescue.

Relief Fund Builds Up

Alongside the physical relief effort, donations have been flowing into Nepal's Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund. The fund had nearly Nepalese rupee 12 billion available as of September 8, according to the Ministry of Finance, Nepal.

Of this, NPR 8.77 billion was in local currency and NPR 3.18 billion equivalent in dollar accounts.

The government reported NPR 9.87 billion was collected since the floods, while NPR 2.08 billion was already available before the disaster.

The government has also transferred NPR 1 billion to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority for the response.
